learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact, cut repeated words, and use a connector (and, but, so, because, which) or a list with commas.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos, elimina las palabras repetidas y usa un conector (and, but, so, because, which) o una lista con comas.
learn.model: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood, and they live in oceans worldwide.
learn.notice: Three short sentences became one. The word octopuses is used only once, and no fact was lost.

items.prompt: Which sentence best combines the two octopus facts?
items.text: Octopuses have three hearts. Octopuses have blue blood.

options.text: Octopuses have three hearts, and octopuses have blue blood.
Octopuses have three hearts blue blood.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.

items.why: The best combination keeps both facts and says octopuses only once. The first choice repeats words and the second is missing a connector.
items.whyEs: La mejor combinación conserva ambos datos y dice octopuses una sola vez. La primera repite palabras y la segunda no tiene conector.

items.prompt: Which combination shows the reason an octopus can squeeze through tiny gaps?
items.text: Octopuses can squeeze through tiny gaps. Octopuses have no bones.

options.text: Octopuses can squeeze through tiny gaps, but they have no bones.
Octopuses can squeeze through tiny gaps because they have no bones.
Octopuses can squeeze through tiny gaps, so they have no bones.

items.why: Having no bones is the reason it can squeeze through, so because is the connector that keeps the meaning. So would reverse the cause.
items.whyEs: No tener huesos es la razón por la que puede pasar por espacios pequeños, así que because mantiene el significado. So invertiría la causa.

items.prompt: Choose the connector that keeps the meaning.
parts: Octopuses can change the color of their skin,
they can blend in with rocks and coral.
items.model: Octopuses can change the color of their skin, so they can blend in with rocks and coral.
items.why: Changing color lets an octopus blend in with rocks and coral, which is a result. So connects a cause to its result.
items.whyEs: Cambiar de color le permite al pulpo mimetizarse con las rocas y el coral, lo cual es un resultado. So conecta una causa con su resultado.

items.prompt: Choose the word that joins the giant Pacific octopus facts.
parts: can weigh over 100 pounds, lives in cold waters.
items.model: The giant Pacific octopus, which can weigh over 100 pounds, lives in cold waters.
items.why: Which adds an extra fact about a thing or animal. Use commas around the which phrase, and use who only for people.
items.whyEs: Which agrega un dato extra sobre una cosa o un animal. Usa comas alrededor de la frase con which, y usa who solo para personas.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that keeps all three octopus facts: three hearts, blue blood, and living in oceans worldwide.

options.text: Octopuses live in oceans worldwide, and they have three hearts and blue blood.
Octopuses live in oceans worldwide and have three hearts.
Octopuses, which live in oceans worldwide, have three hearts and blue blood.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
Octopuses have three hearts, have blue blood, and live in oceans worldwide.

items.why: A good combination keeps every fact. Two of the choices leave out a fact, so they are shorter but not complete.
items.whyEs: Una buena combinación conserva todos los datos. Dos de las opciones omiten un dato, así que son más cortas pero no están completas.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines the three den facts without repeating words?
items.text: The octopus hides in a den. The octopus comes out at night. The octopus hunts crabs.

options.text: The octopus hides in a den, the octopus comes out at night, and the octopus hunts crabs.
The octopus hides in a den comes out at night hunts crabs.
The octopus hides in a den, comes out at night, and hunts crabs.

items.why: One subject with three verbs in a list avoids repeating the octopus. Commas and the word and keep the list clear.
items.whyEs: Un solo sujeto con tres verbos en una lista evita repetir the octopus. Las comas y la palabra and mantienen clara la lista.

write.prompt: Combine the three sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep all the facts.
write.promptEs: Combina las tres oraciones en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: The giant Pacific octopus lives in cold water. It hides in rocky dens. It hunts crabs and clams.

Usé palabras clave de las oraciones
I kept the facts from the other sentences
Conservé los datos de las otras oraciones
I wrote at least 12 words
Escribí al menos 12 palabras
I ended with a period
Terminé con un punto

familyTalk.en: Take three short sentences about your day and join them into one, like 'We cooked, ate, and cleaned.'
familyTalk.es: Tomen tres oraciones cortas sobre su día y únanlas en una, como 'We cooked, ate, and cleaned.'

teacherTip.en: Have students count how many words they cut when combining; fewer repeated words usually means a smoother sentence.
teacherTip.es: Pide que cuenten cuántas palabras eliminaron al combinar; menos palabras repetidas suele significar una oración más fluida.

sets.title: The Great Wall in One Sentence
sets.titleEs: La Gran Muralla en una oración

learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact, cut repeated words, and use a connector (and, but, so, because, which) or a list with commas.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos, elimina las palabras repetidas y usa un conector (and, but, so, because, which) o una lista con comas.
learn.model: Many sections of the Great Wall were built by different dynasties, and the Ming Dynasty's sections are the best known.
learn.notice: Two facts are joined with and. The Great Wall is named only once, and no fact is lost.

items.prompt: Which sentence best combines the two facts about Chinese rulers?
items.text: Chinese rulers built walls to protect their borders. Chinese rulers rebuilt the walls over many centuries.

options.text: Chinese rulers built walls to protect their borders, and Chinese rulers rebuilt the walls over many centuries.
Chinese rulers built walls to protect their borders rebuilt over many centuries.
Chinese rulers built walls to protect their borders and rebuilt them over many centuries.

items.why: The best sentence uses one subject with two verbs and replaces the walls with them. No fact is lost and nothing repeats.
items.whyEs: La mejor oración usa un solo sujeto con dos verbos y reemplaza the walls con them. No se pierde ningún dato y nada se repite.

items.prompt: Which combination keeps the correct cause for the Ming Dynasty sentence?
items.text: The Ming Dynasty strengthened the Great Wall. Northern invaders still threatened the empire.

options.text: The Ming Dynasty strengthened the Great Wall, so northern invaders still threatened the empire.
The Ming Dynasty strengthened the Great Wall because northern invaders still threatened the empire.
The Ming Dynasty strengthened the Great Wall, northern invaders still threatened the empire.

items.why: The threat is the reason for strengthening the wall, so because fits. The first choice reverses cause and result, and the last is a comma splice.
items.whyEs: La amenaza es la razón para reforzar la muralla, así que because encaja. La primera invierte causa y resultado, y la última es una coma que une dos oraciones.

items.prompt: Choose the connector that keeps the meaning.
parts: it could not stop every attack.
items.model: The wall slowed invaders, but it could not stop every attack.
items.why: The wall helped, yet it did not stop everything. That is a contrast, so but is the right connector.
items.whyEs: La muralla ayudó, pero no detuvo todo. Eso es un contraste, así que but es el conector correcto.

items.prompt: Choose the word that joins the watchtower facts.
parts: were built along the wall, let soldiers send signals with smoke and fire.
items.model: Watchtowers, which were built along the wall, let soldiers send signals with smoke and fire.
items.why: Which adds extra information about the watchtowers. Commas go before and after the which phrase.
items.whyEs: Which agrega información extra sobre las torres de vigilancia. Las comas van antes y después de la frase con which.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that keeps all three Great Wall facts: it is thousands of miles long, different dynasties built sections, and the Ming Dynasty built the best-known sections.

options.text: The Great Wall, which stretches thousands of miles, includes sections built by different dynasties, and the Ming Dynasty built the best-known ones.
The Great Wall stretches thousands of miles, and the Ming Dynasty built it.
Different dynasties built many sections of the Great Wall, which stretches thousands of miles, and the Ming Dynasty built the best-known sections.
The Great Wall stretches thousands of miles and many sections were built by different dynasties.

items.why: The right choices carry all three facts. The others drop the fact about the Ming Dynasty or change the meaning.
items.whyEs: Las opciones correctas incluyen los tres datos. Las otras omiten el dato de la dinastía Ming o cambian el significado.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines the three building materials without repeating words?
items.text: The wall was built of stone. The wall was built of brick. The wall was built of packed earth.

options.text: The wall was built of stone, the wall was built of brick, and the wall was built of packed earth.
The wall was built of stone, brick, and packed earth.
The wall was built of stone brick and packed earth.

items.why: A list of three items needs commas, and the repeated words the wall was built of are used only once.
items.whyEs: Una lista de tres elementos necesita comas, y las palabras repetidas the wall was built of se usan una sola vez.

write.prompt: Combine the three sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep all the facts.
write.promptEs: Combina las tres oraciones en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: Many travelers visit the Great Wall. The wall is very old. Some sections are in good condition.

familyTalk.en: Pick a place you have visited. Join three short facts about it into one sentence.
familyTalk.es: Elijan un lugar que hayan visitado. Unan tres datos cortos sobre él en una sola oración.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to check that each fact from the original sentences still appears somewhere in the combined sentence.
teacherTip.es: Pide que verifiquen que cada dato de las oraciones originales aparezca todavía en la oración combinada.

learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una sola oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos, elimina las palabras repetidas y usa un conector (and, but, so, because, which) o una lista con comas.
learn.model: A rectangle has four right angles, and its opposite sides are equal in length.
learn.notice: Two facts about the same shape share one sentence. The word rectangle appears once and its replaces the second mention.

items.prompt: Which sentence best combines the two facts about squares?
items.text: A square has four equal sides. A square has four right angles.

options.text: A square has four equal sides, a square has four right angles.
A square has four equal sides four right angles.
A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

items.why: The best combination uses and to join both facts and says a square only once.
items.whyEs: La mejor combinación usa and para unir ambos datos y dice a square una sola vez.

items.prompt: Which sentence best combines the two cyclist facts?
items.text: A cyclist rides at a constant speed of 12 miles per hour. The cyclist rides for 3 hours.

options.text: The cyclist rides at a constant speed of 12 miles per hour because the cyclist rides for 3 hours.
The cyclist rides at a constant speed of 12 miles per hour for 3 hours.
The cyclist rides at a constant speed of 12 miles per hour, but the cyclist rides for 3 hours.

items.why: The second fact adds how long, so it fits as a phrase at the end. Because and but add a reason or contrast that is not in the facts.
items.whyEs: El segundo dato agrega cuánto tiempo, así que encaja como frase al final. Because y but agregan una razón o un contraste que no está en los datos.

items.prompt: Choose the connector that keeps the meaning.
parts: A prime number has exactly two factors,
a composite number has more than two.
items.model: A prime number has exactly two factors, but a composite number has more than two.
items.why: The sentence compares two different kinds of numbers, so a contrast word is needed. But shows the difference.
items.whyEs: La oración compara dos tipos distintos de números, así que se necesita una palabra de contraste. But muestra la diferencia.

items.prompt: Choose the word that joins the facts about 12.
parts: is a composite number, has six factors.
items.model: The number 12, which is a composite number, has six factors.
items.why: Which adds an extra fact about the number 12. Commas go before and after the which phrase.
items.whyEs: Which agrega un dato extra sobre el número 12. Las comas van antes y después de la frase con which.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that keeps all three facts: a rectangle is a parallelogram, a parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides, and a rectangle has four right angles.

options.text: A rectangle is a parallelogram with four right angles, and it has two pairs of parallel sides.
A rectangle has four right angles and a parallelogram.
A rectangle, a parallelogram with two pairs of parallel sides, has four right angles.
A rectangle has four right angles and two pairs of parallel sides, and a parallelogram has four right angles.

items.why: The right choices keep all three facts and stay true. The others are confusing or say something that is not accurate about parallelograms.
items.whyEs: Las opciones correctas conservan los tres datos y siguen siendo verdaderas. Las otras confunden o dicen algo que no es cierto sobre los paralelogramos.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines the three actions without repeating words?
items.text: Pablo solved the equation. Pablo checked his answer. Pablo found a mistake.

options.text: Pablo solved the equation, Pablo checked his answer, and Pablo found a mistake.
Pablo solved the equation checked his answer found a mistake.
Pablo solved the equation, checked his answer, and found a mistake.

items.why: One subject, three verbs in a list. Commas separate the actions, and Pablo is not repeated.
items.whyEs: Un sujeto, tres verbos en una lista. Las comas separan las acciones y Pablo no se repite.
